description: Doubles (quadruples...) the frequency of each waveset IN PLACE: every waveset is replaced by 2^mult compressed copies of itself, transposing perceived pitch up mult octaves while the duration stays put - waveset-domain octave-up without resampling artifacts or length change. FFT-verified: a 440 Hz tone renders at exactly 880 Hz at mult 1 (1696 Hz at mult 2 - slight quantisation wobble). Duration static: -0.1% at mult 1 (tones/flat noise/sweep), +3.6% at mult 2 on a tone (waveset re-quantisation) - budget more at higher mult. Deterministic, no other parameters. Part of the distmore suite (bright / double / segsbkwd / segszig). MONO only.
musical_use: Instant octave-up shimmer that keeps the timeline: because each waveset is squeezed and repeated within its own slot, transients stay where they were - great on percussive and vocal material where a resampler would smear timing. mult 1 is the musical sweet spot (clean octave with a slight waveset glassiness); 2-4 push into whistle/ring territory as quantisation artifacts stack. Classic uses: parallel octave layer under the dry signal, or chained with distort envel/reverse to build glassy waveset counterpoint. For downward octaves use distort divide (curated).

mult.description: Octave steps up (CDP-enforced 1-4: 5 refused 'Parameter[1] Value (5.000000) out of range (1.000000 to 4.000000)'). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 ... brkpnt_files not permitted.') - render steps for evolving transposition.

examples.expected_use: 440 Hz reads as 880 Hz, same length (-0.1%); mix under the dry sound for shimmer.
Pitch x4 with audible waveset glass; expect up to ~4% length drift on periodic sources.

known_issues: SEGFAULT ON UNIPOLAR MATERIAL (first-class): a positive-only click train (no zero crossings) crashes the binary outright - exit 139, Segmentation fault, no error message, no output. Gate or verify material with real zero crossings first.
Duration drift grows with mult (+3.6% at 2 on a 440 Hz tone; -0.1% at 1) - waveset re-quantisation; the pinned row uses mult 1 on flat noise (-0.005%).
